source: EmulatorX.dll (Emulator X3, 2008-09-14). Filter-class dispatch table at 0x1806d5f80, 32-byte records; class names are the MSVC RTTI names reached through each record's descriptor pointer. Within a record the descriptor belongs to the compile function of the following record; that one-record shift is verified at both ends of the table, by CPhantomFilterP2k resolving to FUN_1802d3ce0 (the bank reader named in ghidra_extracts/runtime_hacks.md) and CPhantomLP2Pole to FUN_1802c4b80.
mapping_basis: Filter names are matched to classes by order and type, which is unambiguous for the pole-count and EQ classes. BlissBatz to CPhantomBatman is positional: it is the remaining entry in the PhazeShift1/PhazeShift2/BlissBatz/FlangerLite run, which the dispatch table holds in the same order as Phaser1/Phaser2/Batman/Flanger1.
rate_slots: Each filter occupies four consecutive table slots, one per rate. For the 33 stored skins the four are one design pre-warped: every live pole of bank n is an exact scaling of bank 0 by 44100/rate, 31 of 31 skins on every bank, sd 1e-4. For the 17 closed-form primitives they are distinct designs per rate, because base[] and slope[] are not proportional across rates; 0 of 7 testable primitives fall in the scaling family. The X3 xStream law describes the primitives, not the skins.

rom_table.provenance: Stored. A table read with no arithmetic on the words.

closed_form.provenance: Computed. Closed-form integer arithmetic over a descriptor plus per-rate base and slope tables.

morph.provenance: Computed from user-set endpoints. Emulator X only; absent from the Proteus 2000 ROM filter table.

law.note: Radius is an affine function of frequency. Morph Designer's rad = ((freq * 0x7c) >> 8) + 0x76 is the same law with different constants: in word units 440*byte + 4608 against 442*byte + 4896. Neither compiler carries a per-section volume term; the shared writer emits the constant 0xdfff as the fifth word.
